newsitem.title: HONG KONG: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS - Philippines tops the news.
newsitem.headline: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS - Philippines tops the news.

text.p: The Philippines figured prominently in Asian debt markets on Tuesday, with PLDT roadshowing its bond and the central bank choosing lead managers for its much-awaited issue.
The central bank announced that Salomon Brothers has won the right to lead manage the Philippines' Yankee bond scheduled for launch in the second quarter of this year.
Central Bank Governor Gabriel Singson said that the target maturity for the bonds shall be a minimum of 30 years and that a portion of the issue would have a maturity of 100 years.
The size will be between US$750 million and US$1.0 billion.
J.P. Morgan, Citicorp, Merrill Lynch, Morgan Stanley and ING Barings will act as co-lead managers. The bonds will be fully registered with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission.

The bonds will provide a new benchmark for Philippine borrowers while extending the country's yield curve. The Philippines currently has a 20-year bond outstanding that was launched as part of its exchange of Brady bonds last year.
The Philippines Long Distance Telephone Co (PLDT) showcased its upcoming US$200 million global bond issue in Hong Kong today in its only Asian roadshow.
Over 100 investors attended the Hong Kong gathering.
Goldman Sachs and Citicorp International are lead managers.
Presentations will be made in London and New York before the bond's launch, which is expected in the week of February 24.
The issue had been widely rumoured to be a structured transaction.

Bankers had said that one of the possible structures suggested for the bond would have allowed the issuer to reduce the coupon in the event PLDT's credit ratings were upgraded by the major agencies. In the early stages of its life, the bond would have paid a premium.

PLDT currently is rated equally with the sovereign at Ba2 by Moody's Investors Service and BB by Standard and Poor's Corp. Moody's said last month that it may raise the Philippines' credit rating in the light of the successful macro-economic policies implemented by the government in recent years.
However, now it appears that the PLDT bond will be a straight issue. Terms have not been finalized, but the bond is expected to have a long maturity of 10 years or more.
"It's easier for investors to understand that sort of credit with a simple structure," remarked one banker.
Because of the long tenor, a large share of the bond is expected to place in the U.S.. The bond will be fully registered with the SEC.
Like many other international carriers, PLDT will be affected by an impending cut in U.S. telephone rates and by increased competition.
The company announced on Monday that it is reducing its staff by 1,800 people to 16,473 by the end of this month to trim costs and that more cuts are expected in coming years.
PLDT also proposes to restructure its tariff system to reflect the expected change in revenue flows from international and local calls.

"We have to do this to maintain our market strength. We have to change our (rate structure) because we are vulnerable to long distance calls," executive vice president Edgardo del Fonso told reporters in Manila on Monday.

Elsewhere, co-arranger groups for loan financings of Hong Kong borrowers Hysan Development, Cheung Kong and Kerry Holdings are expected to be in place by the end of this week. General syndication of the loans will follow shortly thereafter.

A roadshow for QPL International's US$100 million floating rate note issue will be held on Wednesday in Hong Kong, bankers said. The five-year paper has puts in year three and is expected to pay a return of 150-160 basis points over the London Interbank Offered Rate.
